info.name: FoodDeliveryService
info.description:
Two top-level folders: `AuthService` (auth flow tests against auth-service) and `DeliveryService` (delivery-service tests against the delivery-scoping rule in DeliveryService.findAll).

`AuthService`: superadmin login/logout, superadmin creating one staff account per role (restaurant_admin, restaurant_employee, delivery_admin, delivery_driver), login/logout for each created account, and scoped staff creation (restaurant_admin creating a restaurant_employee, delivery_admin creating a delivery_driver) verifying AuthService.assertCanCreate.

`DeliveryService`: self-contained re-logins as DELIVERY_ADMIN/DELIVERY_DRIVER (independent of whether AuthService's own role folders already logged out) followed by `GET /deliveries` — verifies DELIVERY_ADMIN sees every delivery while DELIVERY_DRIVER only ever sees deliveries assigned to itself (DeliveryOrderRepository.findAllByDriverId).

Note: auth-service has no `/auth/logout` endpoint — JWT auth is stateless (see PROJECT_CONTEXT.md "Planned Refactoring": a future access-token/refresh-token rework will add real server-side logout). Until then, "logout" only means discarding the client-held token, exactly like `authLogout()` in api-tester.html. Every Logout request here validates the token is currently active, then clears the collection variable that holds it.

Run order: `AuthService > Superadmin` must run first (creates the staff accounts and captures their generated emails/userId); everything else — the four `AuthService` role folders, the two `DeliveryService` role folders, and the three `RestaurantService` role folders — can then run in any order, though running `OrderService` first (to place a real order) lets `RestaurantService > Restaurant Employee`'s order-status test drive a genuinely fresh restaurant order instead of falling back to whatever restaurant orders already exist for Bella Italia.

`RestaurantService`: role-based authorization checks against restaurant-service, analogous to `DeliveryService`'s role folders. `Restaurant Admin` self-contained re-login followed by a full create → read → update → delete cycle for both a restaurant and one of its menu items (RestaurantService.assertCallerIsAdmin allows SUPER_ADMIN/RESTAURANT_ADMIN). `Restaurant Employee` self-contained re-login followed by: allowed GET/PATCH of restaurant orders (RestaurantOrderService.assertCallerManagesRestaurantOrders allows restaurant staff) and allowed GET of restaurants (unrestricted), plus forbidden (403) restaurant/menu-item create/update/delete calls (RestaurantService.assertCallerIsAdmin rejects RESTAURANT_EMPLOYEE). `Customer` self-contained re-login followed by a forbidden (403) GET of restaurant orders, proving non-staff roles are blocked from that endpoint while still able to browse restaurants/menu-items.
